options: The Wav2Vec2Model takes a raw audio waveform and converts it into input_values (which are normalized and padded).
The Wav2Vec2Processor takes a raw audio waveform and converts it into input_values (which are normalized and padded).
Both Wav2Vec2Model and Wav2Vec2Processor involve deep neural networks in their architectures.
Like BERT, Wav2Vec2 applies masked learning to the audio representations.
Wav2Vec2 processes audio in a left-to-right manner like GPT (which uses CLM).

questions.text: You transcribed an audio recording using Whisper and applied speaker diarization. However, you notice that the transcribed text is accurate, but the speaker labels frequently change mid- sentence, even when the same person is speaking. Which of the following are definite causes of this issue?
options: The speaker segments are too short, causing the clustering model to misclassify speakers.
Whisper does not support speaker diarization, so the labels are randomly assigned.
The timestamps from Whisper do not align with the diarization output, leading to incorrect speaker switching.
The transcription model has misrecognized words, which affects speaker identification.
correct_answer: The speaker segments are too short, causing the clustering model to misclassify speakers.
The timestamps from Whisper do not align with the diarization output, leading to incorrect speaker switching.

correct_answer: It loads a large pre-trained Whisper model for transcription.
It splits the audio into segments and returns the transcribed text.

questions.text: A speaker diarization pipeline typically consists of multiple components. Which of the following components are essential in a speaker diarization system?
options: Voice Activity Detection (VAD) to remove non-speech segments.
Speaker Embedding Extraction (e.g., ECAPA-TDNN, x-vectors) to represent speaker characteristics.
Speech-to-Text Transcription to convert spoken words into text.
Clustering (e.g., Agglomerative Clustering, K-Means) to group similar speaker embeddings.
Automatic Language Identification (ALI) to detect the spoken language.
correct_answer: Voice Activity Detection (VAD) to remove non-speech segments.
Speaker Embedding Extraction (e.g., ECAPA-TDNN, x-vectors) to represent speaker characteristics.
Clustering (e.g., Agglomerative Clustering, K-Means) to group similar speaker embeddings.

questions.text: What is the primary input format required for fine-tuning SpeechT5?
options: Raw speech waveforms only.
Speaker embeddings only.
A combination of text and speaker embeddings.
MFCC features extracted from audio.
questions.correct_answer: A combination of text and speaker embeddings.

questions.text: What additional preprocessing is required when fine-tuning SpeechT5 on low-resource languages?
options: Use phoneme-based tokenization instead of direct text tokenization.
Train on speaker embeddings that include multiple dialects.
Convert all text to uppercase for better model accuracy.
Increase the hidden size of the transformer layers to accommodate new languages.
correct_answer: Use phoneme-based tokenization instead of direct text tokenization.
Train on speaker embeddings that include multiple dialects.
